## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a2b90f7fb082b83e0366a6220d17a83abcb9f9df`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json, skills/objectstack-data/references/seeds.md + none
Security-touching: no

PR #36800 for card #36122. Inputs read: the card body and its 3 comments (triage 7065150451, claim 7112521029, dev report 7118134435), the PR body, its 3-file list, its 2 thread comments, the net diff against `main` (merge-base bbc7e037f3, +12/-2) and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built, run or checked out.

Remainder of the diff, not reviewed here (the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`): `.changeset/36122-seeds-rollup-never-stored.md`, read only for ②.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged. The diff edits one sentence of skill prose and one `expected_output` string. No schema, validator, lint rule, loader or error code is touched, so nothing an author writes is newly accepted or newly refused. Right.
- Public surface: the published `@objectstack/skills` bundle changes by one sentence in `objectstack-data/references/seeds.md`. The rule an author follows ("never seed the roll-up") is the same before and after; only its stated reason changes. Right.
- Eval surface: case 32 keeps its `prompt`, `must_contain` (`defineSeed`, `invoice: 'INV-1'`) and `must_not_contain` (`amount_paid: 4800`, `amount_paid: 2000`). The machine-checked assertions therefore accept and refuse exactly the answers they did on `main`; only the judged prose moves. Right.
- Skill size: the PR body reads `seeds.md` at 1898 tokens against a ceiling of 1898, with no ceiling moved and the ratchet script not in the diff. The file list confirms the script is not edited. The `Lint · docs & code guards` check-run concluded success on this head.
- Check-runs on this head at the time of this record: 19 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 6 still in progress (`Build Core`, `Test Core (1/10)`, `Test Core (2/10)`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`). Those six carry no verdict yet. This record does not stand in for them: the landing still waits on every check green.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/skills` (the package exists at `packages/skills/package.json`; five earlier skill-text changesets on `main` carry the same level). The diff publishes a wording fix to shipped skill text with no accept-set change, so `patch` is the right level. `Check Changeset` concluded success.

Clause-②: no — stated on the PR body, the changeset and the claim, and it matches the diff: nothing that was accepted is refused, and nothing an author already wrote behaves differently because of this PR. The behaviour change itself shipped in #36118.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report. Nothing to answer.
- Dev deviations (report 7118134435): one merge of `main` on the branch with none of its commits on the claimed files (confirmed: the net diff is the 3 claimed files); a 2-byte trim in a second commit; five build-dependent gates left to CI; the PR body opening with the `Fixes` line and no seat signature; model-free commit trailers; the worktree kept. None bears on the contract. The five gates left to CI fall in check-runs that are either green or still running, as listed in ①.
- File surface: the diff stays inside the claim (seeds.md, the one eval file, one changeset). No breach.
- Seat ACCEPT 7118161122 routes the PR as Tier H because the eval path has "security" in its name. Answer on the question this record owns: the changed hunk (case 32) teaches seed loading against a validation rule and a roll-up. It teaches no permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour, and neither does the seeds.md sentence. Hence `Security-touching: no`. Which landing arm then applies is the seat's and the queue guard's call, not this record's.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no code in the diff, so no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`skills/objectstack-data/references/seeds.md`** — new sentence: "Never seed the roll-up: a seeded `amount_paid` is never stored (a warning per dataset); the child rows compute it." Read against `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts` on `main` (identical at the PR head, the file is not in the diff):

- "never stored": `summaryFieldNames` (l.794-801) returns every field with `type === 'summary'`, whatever the aggregate and whether or not it is `readonly`. The record loop (l.2304-2311) deletes each such key from the record copy before the replay compare, the insert and the update. So the value reaches neither the engine write nor any validation rule. Holds.
- "a warning per dataset": one `logger.warn` after the record loop (l.3268-3277), only when at least one value was taken out, naming the object, the fields and the count. No error is pushed and no load-result key carries it. Holds.
- "the child rows compute it": the engine starts the column at its empty-child-list value and recomputes from child writes (`summaryFieldsLockedOnWrite` note in `packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`, which itself says a seed load never sends a roll-up value because of #35655). Holds.
- The kept sentence on record order ("a rule reading a parent roll-up sees the total earlier rows left") is untouched and is now the only reason a payment seed can be refused, which is the model the card asked for.
- The old reason ("stored as written, and a cap on payments refuses those it counts") is gone from the file. A search of `skills/`, `ui/skills/` and `content/docs/` at the PR head finds no other place that still says a seeded roll-up is stored.

Attempts to break it:

- Another seed write door that skips the strip: `packages/runtime/src/seed-loader.ts` is a 9-line re-export of the same `SeedLoaderService`. Every seed path goes through the loop above. No second door found.
- A roll-up contributed by an object extension: the strip reads the resolved definition, which is the engine's merged schema, so it is covered.
- A definition the loader cannot resolve: the loader then declares no summary fields and writes the record as authored (stated in the `summaryFieldNames` jsdoc). This is a load whose object is not defined at all. It is outside the scenario the sentence teaches (an author seeding an object they declared with a roll-up), so "never" holds for the reader the sentence addresses. Not a finding.
- `null` versus `undefined`: an explicit `null` counts as a supplied value and is warned about; an `undefined` key is removed silently. Both are never stored. Consistent with the sentence.

**`skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json`** (case 32) — judged against the card's ask ("update the evals that exercise seeding roll-ups to match") and the sentence above:

- The new `expected_output` says the loader "never stores a supplied `amount_paid` (it leaves the value out of the write and logs one warning per dataset naming the fields)". Each clause matches the code read above.
- It adds a negative line: the answer must not say a seeded `amount_paid` is stored or makes the rule refuse the payments. This is the old model, and refusing it is what the card is for.
- The answer shape the case accepts is unchanged: invoice rows without the roll-up, payments by natural key, each fitting what earlier rows left, the rule not weakened, validation rules not described as skipped. An answer written from the new seeds.md reaches it.
- The dev's claim that case 32 is the only data-skill eval that seeds a roll-up: the search at the PR head for `amount_paid` and roll-up seeding wording under `skills/` hits case 32 and seeds.md only. Holds.

N1 (nit) — case 32's `expected_output` says the warning names the fields; seeds.md says only "a warning per dataset". The detail is true to the code and sits in a parenthesis that explains why the invoice rows carry no roll-up, so a correct answer is not required to recite it. Left as an accepted deviation; no change asked on this head.
